nodes.name: CFP Acid Activation
nodes.procedure: The clean carbon paper was firstly soaked in 1.0 M HNO3 for 30 min, and then activated by CV in 0.5 M H2SO4 electrolyte solution for five cycles (scan range 0.2–1.5 V vs. RHE) using a three-electrode setup.
nodes.source_text: Before electrodeposition, the clean carbon paper undergoes a pre-activation process: the clean carbon paper was firstly soaked in 1.0 M HNO3 for 30 min, and then activated by CV in 0.5 M H2SO4 electrolyte solution for five cycles...

nodes.name: UPED Synthesis UP-RuNiSAs/C
nodes.procedure: A three-electrode setup was used (saturated Ag|AgCl reference, Pt wire counter, CFP working electrode). 100 mL plating solution containing NiCl2·6H2O (150 mM), RuCl3·xH2O (5 mM), H3BO3 (160 mM), NH4Cl (20 mM), PVP (1.0 g) had pH adjusted to 2.7 with NH3·H2O. UPED at -0.8 V vs Ag|AgCl for 4000 pulses (8000 s) gave catalyst loading of 1.25 mg/cm².

unit_operations.name: Electrode setup
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: A three-electrode attached to an ECLab electrochemical workstation set-up was used... CFP electrode (1 cm × 1 cm) as working electrode.

unit_operations.name: Plating bath preparation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: 100 mL of plating solution was prepared, which contains NiCl2·6H2O (150 mM), RuCl3·xH2O (5 mM), H3BO3 (160 mM), NH4Cl (20 mM), PVP (1.0 g). The pH was adjusted to 2.7 using the NH3·H2O

unit_operations.name: Unipolar pulse electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: UPED method with pulse voltage of -0.8 V (vs. Ag|AgCl) for 4000 times of pulses (8000 s). The catalyst loading mass was decided to be 1.25 mg cm⁻²

nodes.source_text: Synthesis of UP-RuNiSAs/C. A three-electrode attached to an ECLab electrochemical workstation set-up was used... The UP-·RuNiSAs/C was obtained by UPED method with pulse voltage of -0.8 V (vs. Ag|AgCl) for 4000 times of pulses (8000 s).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show diffraction peaks corresponding to Ru (PDF no. 06-0633) with broad peaks indicating tiny particle size of Ru particles for UP-RuNiSAs/C; no diffraction signal of Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the UP-RuNi SAs / C and CP-RuNi/C (Fig. 3a and Supplementary Figs. 20–21) show the diffraction peaks corresponding to the Ru (PDF no. 06-0633), with the tiny particle size of Ru particles for UP-·RuNi SAs / C evident from the broad peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show agglomerate-like particles of about 2 μm in size uniformly loaded on the carbon substrate for UP-RuNiSAs/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As indicated in Fig. 3b and Supplementary Fig. 22a of the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images, agglomerate-like particles of about 2 μm in size were uniformly loaded on the carbon substrate...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image shows nanocrystalline size of about 2 nm for UP-RuNiSAs/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image and the corresponding size distribution plot (Fig. 3c) further demonstrated that the size of the nanocrystalline is about 2 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM displays lattice fringes of 0.214 nm corresponding to the (002) crystal plane of hexagonal Ru for UP-RuNiSAs/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3d, the UP-·RuNi SAs / C displayed lattice fringes of 0.214 nm, corresponding to the (002) crystal plane of hexagonal Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-STEM reveals uniform dispersion of bright spots indicating high-contrast single atoms (Ni SAs) on carbon fiber paper and Ru nanocrystals with exposed (002) surface for UP-RuNiSAs/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru nanocrystals can be accurately distinguished and identified using spherical aberration correction scanning TEM (AC-STEM). Figure 3e revealed the uniform dispersion of bright spots, indicating the uniform distribution of high-contrast single atoms on carbon fiber paper (CFP).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS mapping shows Ru element uniformly dispersed at nanocrystal position and Ni element uniformly dispersed around substrate and Ru for UP-RuNiSAs/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Fig. 3g, it can be observed that Ru element is uniformly dispersed at the position of the nanocrystal, while Ni element is uniformly dispersed around the substrate and Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES reveals atomic ratios of 92.32/7.68 for Ru/Ni in UP-RuNiSAs/C and 81.73/18.27 in CP-RuNi/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) accurately analyzed the Ru and Ni contents in the catalysts, revealing atomic ratios of 92.32/7.68 for Ru/Ni in UP-·RuNi SAs / C and 81.73/18.27 in CP-RuNi/C respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES and EXAFS confirm atomic dispersion of Ni with Ni-C coordination and no Ni-Ni or Ni-Ru bonding in UP-RuNiSAs/C; Ru K-edge shows Ru-Ru coordination with decreased coordination number due to nano effect.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We conducted X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) at Ni K-edge of UP-·RuNi SAs / C to expound the single atom dispersion of Ni... The above results confirm that Ni is anchored to carbon in UP-RuNi SAs / C.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni²⁺ at 856.1 eV and 873.9 eV, no Ni⁰ peak, Ru⁰ at 462.15 eV and 484.13 eV, Ru⁴⁺ at 464.09 eV and 486.48 eV with positive shifts indicating electron transfer from Ru to Ni in UP-RuNiSAs/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fitted Ni 2p spectrum of the UP-·RuNi SAs / C (Fig. 4f) shows the valences of Ni²⁺ at 856.1 eV and 873.9 eV due to surface oxidation... implying that electrons transferred from Ru to Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows significantly higher carbon defects for UP-RuNiSAs/C compared to CP-RuNi/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Surprisingly, the scale of carbon defects for UP-RuNi SAs / C was significantly fuller than that of CP-RuNi/C certified in Fig. 4h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double layer capacitance Cdl calculated as 292.06 mF/cm² from CV at different scan rates, corresponding to ECSA of 584.5 m²/g for UP-RuNiSAs/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The calculated double layer capacitance (Cdl) value (Supplementary Fig. 44) of UP-·RuNi SAs / C according to the cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves at different scan rates (Supplementary Fig. 45) proved to be the highest (292.06 mF cm⁻²), leading to the higher ECSA value of 584.5 m² g⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows lowest charge transfer resistance Rct of 0.10 Ω and 0.12 Ω for UP-RuNiSAs/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS)... in which the UP-RuNiSAs/C exhibited the lowest charge transfer internal resistances (Rct) of 0.10 Ω and 0.12 Ω.
